ff11.note: Japanese and English clients share the same game data; names taken from the Windower resource dump of the client's spell table (ja/en fields).

ff14.note: Global client; names taken from the game Action sheet via XIVAPI (Japanese and English fields of the same row).

kh.release: Kingdom Hearts (PS2, 2002 NA); same names in Kingdom Hearts Final Mix in HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX (PS4 2017, PC 2021)
kh.note: Spell and summon names did not change between the original English release and the HD ReMIX.

ff.release: Final Fantasy V Pixel Remaster (PC/mobile 2021, PS4/Switch 2023)
ff.note: Series representative is Final Fantasy V. Pixel Remaster names are identical to Final Fantasy V Advance (GBA, 2006) for all mapped spells; Final Fantasy Anthology (PS, 1999) names go in older. Wiki pages were read through search-engine extracts because the wiki blocked direct fetching.

ff1.note: Pixel Remaster spell names (Caves of Narshe PR list) are the same as Dawn of Souls (GBA 2004) / 20th Anniversary (PSP 2007). Older names: NES (1990) and Final Fantasy Origins (PS, 2003).

ff2.release: Final Fantasy II Pixel Remaster (PC/mobile 2021, PS4/Switch 2023)
ff2.note: Pixel Remaster names match Dawn of Souls (GBA 2004) / 20th Anniversary (PSP 2007); older is Final Fantasy Origins (PS, 2003).

ff3.release: Final Fantasy III Pixel Remaster (PC/mobile 2021, PS4/Switch 2023)
ff3.note: The Famicom original was never released in English. The Pixel Remaster uses the 3D remake (DS 2006/2008 NA) terms for magic and summon spells, so the names are the same as the DS version.

ff4.release: Final Fantasy IV Pixel Remaster (PC/mobile 2021, PS4/Switch 2023)
ff4.note: 2D line of releases. The 3D remake (DS 2008, PC 2014) uses some different names (e.g. Shadowbind, Mirage) and is not used here.

ff6.release: Final Fantasy VI Pixel Remaster (PC/mobile 2022, PS4/Switch 2023)
ff6.note: The wiki states the 2014 mobile/PC and Pixel Remaster translations are identical to Final Fantasy VI Advance (GBA, 2006/2007) for these terms. Older names are from Final Fantasy III (SNES, 1994), also used in the PS Anthology (1999).

ff7.release: Final Fantasy VII (PS 1997; the same English text is used in the PC, PS4, Switch and Xbox ports)
ff7.note: Not the Remake/Rebirth, which renamed many spells (e.g. Quakera, Manaward, Breach). For summons the wiki translation table gives normalized names (Kujata, Typhon, Knights of the Round); the in-game names Kjata, Typoon and Knights of Round come from Caves of Narshe and Jegged.

ff8.note: The Remastered uses the original 1999 English translation (PS/PC); names were read from the wiki translation table and ability pages.

ff9.release: Final Fantasy IX (PC 2016, PS4 2017, Switch/Xbox One 2019; North American English text of the 2000 PS release)
ff9.note: The European English release differs in a few names (e.g. Frost is Freeze).

ff10.release: Final Fantasy X HD Remaster (Final Fantasy X/X-2 HD Remaster; PS3/Vita 2014, PS4 2015, PC 2016, Switch/Xbox One 2019)
ff10.note: Based on the International version; spell and aeon names are the same as the original 2001 North American release.

ff12.release: Final Fantasy XII The Zodiac Age (PS4 2017, PC 2018, Switch/Xbox One 2019)
ff12.note: Names read from the wiki translation table (Japanese / romaji / English). No name changes from the 2006 PS2 release were reported for these magicks and Espers.

smt.release: Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne HD Remaster (PS4/Switch/PC, 2021)
smt.note: Names matched via the Megami Tensei Wiki Nocturne translation table (Japanese-English); the wiki's HD Remaster skill list marks names changed from the 2004/2005 English release (Shin Megami Tensei: Nocturne / Lucifer's Call, PS2) and none of the mapped spell names changed except where 'older' is given.

persona2.note: The 1999 PS1 original was not released in English; the 2011 PSP remake is the only official English release. スリスティ skipped: sources disagree (Suristi / Sristi).

smt4.note: Mapped from the Megami Tensei Wiki's SMT IV translation table (English / Japanese / romaji); 1 source for each name.
